content:
Opening position for u1.

r1 (must-have, no external services) and r2 (must-have, revocation takes effect on the next request) drive the whole design. I would add POST /auth/login issuing a random opaque token, store the SHA-256 of it locally alongside user_id and an expiry, and resolve it on every request. Logout deletes the row, so r2 is exact rather than eventual. Nothing leaves the box, so r1 holds.

I would carry the token in a session cookie. r3 (nice-to-have) says keep the pytest suite green, so I would add an auth fixture rather than touch the harness.

Opening position for u2.

r4 (must-have, stateless) and r5 (must-have, no cookies) drive mine. I would issue a signed JWT at login carrying user_id and exp, verify it with a local secret on each request, and require it in an Authorization: Bearer header. No shared session store, so any node can verify independently and r4 holds. Header-based, so the mobile client works and r5 holds.

r6 (nice-to-have, sub-5ms) is comfortable — HMAC verification is microseconds with no I/O.

I note claude's proposal is a per-request database lookup behind a cookie. That collides with both of my must-haves.

Conceding r5's mechanism. Holding r1 and r2.

Concede: cookies. u1 never asked for cookies — that was my preference, not a requirement. Moving the token to an Authorization: Bearer header satisfies r5 and costs r1 and r2 nothing. Dropped.

Hold, with reason: r2. A signed JWT is valid until it expires. If u1 revokes a session, gpt's design keeps honouring that token until exp. r2 is marked must-have, so I am not permitted to concede it, and I would not want to — "logged out" meaning "logged out in fifteen minutes" is the bug we are here to avoid.

Direct question on r4: how do you revoke before exp without a shared revocation list? A revocation list is the shared state r4 is trying to eliminate.

Answering the r4/r2 question directly, because it is the real conflict.

I cannot revoke a stateless JWT before exp without a revocation list, and a revocation list is a shared store. claude is right that the stateless framing defeats itself against r2. r2 is a must-have for u1 and I have no override, so I concede the JWT mechanism.

What I do not concede is r4's goal. Compromise: opaque tokens in one locally-indexed table, resolved through a single function. r2 gets exact revocation, r1 gets no external service, r6 stays comfortable on an indexed primary-key lookup. Because every lookup goes through one function, moving that table to Redis later is a swap, not a rewrite.

Condition: the plan records horizontal scale as a deferred concern, not as resolved. And r5 stands — Bearer header, no cookie fallback.

Accepting gpt's compromise. r1, r2, r3 all hold under it.

One thing to nail down before we call this converged, because it is exactly the kind of thing that turns into a merge conflict at 3am: the boundary. I propose `def authenticate_user(token: str) -> User | None` as the single resolution point. I own it and the store behind it. gpt's middleware calls it and never inspects the token format — otherwise gpt's code ends up encoding assumptions about my storage and we collide the moment either side changes.

File ownership to match: I take src/auth/tokens.py and src/auth/store.py. gpt takes src/auth/middleware.py and the routes. Neither of us writes into the other's set.

Agreed on c1 as the boundary and on the file split.

Confirming the trade explicitly so it is on the record: I gave up stateless JWT verification (r4's mechanism) and accepted opaque tokens against a local store, because r2 is a must-have for u1 and stateless cannot satisfy it. claude gave up session cookies and accepted the Bearer header, because r5 is a must-have for u2.

Deferred, not resolved: r4's horizontal-scale goal. The store is single-node today. c1 is the seam that makes that a later swap.

No must-have is unsatisfied. I have nothing left to hold.

tasks.title: Opaque token issuance and revocable token store
tasks.description: POST /auth/login and /auth/logout. Random 256-bit opaque token, SHA-256 hash stored locally with user_id and expiry. Logout deletes the row (r2). No external IdP (r1).

tasks.title: Bearer-header auth middleware
tasks.description: Token from Authorization: Bearer, never a cookie (r5). Resolves via authenticate_user, attaches User to request, 401 on miss.

tasks.title: Scope note routes to the authenticated user
tasks.description: Apply middleware to /notes, filter every query by request.user.id. Existing tests get an auth fixture, not a rewrite (r3).

interface_contracts.name: authenticate_user
interface_contracts.notes: Single lookup point. None for unknown, expired, or revoked. The middleware never inspects token format, so storage can change without touching t2.

interface_contracts.name: tokens
interface_contracts.signature: tokens(token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL)
interface_contracts.notes: Local SQLite, indexed on token_hash, so r6's sub-5ms budget holds on a single node.

concessions.accepted: Opaque tokens resolved against a local store
concessions.reason: r2 (immediate revocation) is a must-have for u1 and is unreachable with stateless JWT without a revocation list, which reintroduces the shared state r4 was avoiding.
r5 (no cookies on mobile) is a must-have for u2, and cookies were claude's preference rather than anything u1 stated.

t3: scope note routes to the authenticated user
